actual_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: full-frame 16:9 cinematic music-video storyboard still, first transport-option flip, concourse-004-v02.
Input reference Image 1: edit target. Preserve the exact camera view, station corridor at left, indigo space and planet at right, graphite/ivory architecture, cyan and amber practical lights, and controlled painted graphic-novel illustration style.
Replace the ENTIRE low white passenger shuttle, including its silhouette and boarding-door interface, with a striking Giger-esque grown biomechanical passenger ship. This is a fundamental shape redesign: a tall sweeping crescent silhouette rising over the berth, charcoal chitin outer structure, pale bone sweeping crescent arches, exposed organic ribbing, sinewy integrated conduits, an asymmetrical curled body with a spined vertical crest and a long hooked taper. The low conventional shuttle, oval cabin, smooth capsule shape, canopy and rows of seats must be gone. The silhouette must read as a tall organic crescent, not the old shuttle with a new surface skin. Maintain plausible large ship scale, dock support and a boardable interior. Show a softly green bioluminescent vertical slit entrance opening into an organic passenger vestibule; connect it naturally to the existing metal boarding ramp, replacing the final portion of the connection as needed. This must read instantly as a docked vessel people can board, not a creature statue. Clean non-gory biomechanical materials. No skulls, teeth, monster face, blood or bodily gore. No new people needed. No text or symbols. Quiet lower strip for later lyrics. No collage.
SCENE-SPECIFIC OVERRIDE: This biomechanical vessel design replaces the ordinary passenger-shuttle design; the station remains architectural metal. Neither the opening spherical personal ship nor its external engine ring is visible. Do not put geodesic grids on station windows.

CONCOURSE SEQUENCE LOCK: Cinematic painted graphic-novel space adventure with fine controlled ink contours, rich illustrated material detail, indigo space, cyan practical lights and warm amber edges. Adult Harper has the established freckled face, hazel-green eyes and short curly auburn hair; keep her adult proportions and identity. She has changed offscreen during pod transit into a practical pod-issue survival coverall: soft warm-gray fabric, roomy long sleeves with gathered cuffs, closed simple collar, plain central fastening, adjustable gray waist belt, slightly loose trousers, low graphite slip-on utility shoes, one tiny unlettered amber rescue tab at the upper arm. No helmet, armor, gloves, swimsuit, costume logos or readable lettering. Station is a worn but welcoming interstellar transport interchange built around a broad segmented graphite ring with ivory inset ribs, tall arching windows, amber floor-edge strips, cyan docking lights and branching radial berths. Interior promenade has dark ribbed arches, warm ivory wall panels and a few distant travelers; its quieter outer service walkway retains the same architecture. The small arrival capsule is the established enclosed ivory-and-graphite ovoid one-seat escape pod, without a large external ring. The discovered personal spacecraft is the established transparent spherical technological field with faint cyan geodesic lines, graphite equatorial band, upper/lower circular platforms, amber rim lights, sparse cyan rectangular lamps and one vertical open aft engine ring with cyan inner arc; never confuse these two craft. Keep only subjects needed for the shot. Each image is one uninterrupted full-frame 16:9 cinematic composition with a quiet bottom strip for later lyrics; no captions, readable words, watermarks, panels or collage.
validation: Visually reviewed: original low shuttle silhouette fully replaced with tall sweeping crescent biomechanical vessel, pale bone arches, charcoal chitin and conduits, green slit vestibule, hooked taper and spined crest. Reads as docked boardable ship. Station camera/corridor, floor, planet and palette preserved. No gore, skulls, text, monster face, or opening spherical ship. Approved first attempt.
